paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this psalm, friend. The voice of the LORD is bigger than anything you've ever stood in front of. David says it is "powerful" and "majestic" (Psalm 29:4), and it breaks cedars and shakes a wilderness (Psalm 29:5, 8). If trees that tall and stubborn can't stand up to it, then I think we can stop acting like we've got it all figured out.

And watch where David puts the LORD in the middle of all that noise: "The LORD sits enthroned over the flood; the LORD is enthroned as King forever" (Psalm 29:10). Floods are the stuff of our worst days, the bills, the bad news, the week that just keeps coming. Over every one of them, the LORD is the King, and the psalm says that doesn't end. That's a lot of peace for a baker to lean on, and I'd tell you that even on my loudest day.

Now here's the part that gets me every time. David started by telling the heavenly beings to give the LORD strength, and he ends with the LORD giving strength to His people. "The LORD gives His people strength; the LORD blesses His people with peace" (Psalm 29:11). The same voice that thunders over the waters has a blessing waiting for you. So give Him the glory, friend, and then go ahead and take the peace.
